items.title: The oxygen you breathe comes from WATER, not CO2
items.claim: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 and water and produces sugar and oxygen. Every chemistry student writes the equation. But the O2 released is not stripped from the CO2 — it comes entirely from splitting water molecules.
items.prompt: How do we know the oxygen comes from water?

options.text: Both water and CO2 contribute oxygen equally
Ruben and Kamen (1941) used the heavy isotope oxygen-18 to label either water or CO2; the released O2 carried the label only when the water was labelled, never when the CO2 was
CO2 is the source of the oxygen

items.reveal:
The light reactions of photosynthesis split water (photolysis) at the oxygen-evolving complex — a manganese-calcium cluster in Photosystem II. Two water molecules are split: 2 H2O -> 4 H+ + 4 e- + O2.

The electrons enter the electron transport chain. The protons contribute to the thylakoid pH gradient (lumen reaches pH ~5, stroma ~8). ATP synthase uses the gradient to make ATP.

The Calvin cycle (in the stroma) uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into sugar. The carbon from CO2 becomes the carbon in glucose. But the oxygen atoms in CO2 mostly end up in carbohydrate, NOT in the released O2.

Oxygen is, from photosynthesis's point of view, a waste product — and arguably the most consequential pollution event in Earth's history (the Great Oxidation Event, ~2.4 billion years ago, killed most anaerobic life).
items.why: The arrow-pushing equation suggests CO2 donates oxygen. The actual chemistry inverts that: water is split, CO2 is reduced, and the oxygen you breathe was once dissolved in a chloroplast.

items.title: Snapdragons disprove Mendel's simplest law in one cross
items.claim: Red snapdragon crossed with white snapdragon. Mendel's dominance rule says: offspring should all be red (or all white). Snapdragon offspring are PINK. The textbook law fails on its very first test.

options.text: Mendel's laws don't apply to plants

Incomplete dominance — heterozygotes show an intermediate phenotype because neither allele fully masks the other; the red allele encodes a pigment enzyme, and one functional copy produces only half as much pigment as two
Pink is a separate allele not from either parent

items.reveal:
Mendel happened to choose seven traits in peas that were all controlled by single genes with full dominance and complete penetrance. Most real traits are not.

Incomplete dominance: heterozygotes show intermediate phenotypes. Pink snapdragons. Pink camellias. Light pink human skin (one functional MC1R copy).

Codominance: both alleles fully expressed simultaneously. Human ABO blood group (a person with A and B alleles has both A and B antigens on red cells).

Epistasis: gene A's effect depends on gene B's genotype. Coat colour in Labradors (E gene controls whether B gene's brown/black is visible at all).

Polygenic inheritance: traits like height controlled by hundreds of small-effect genes. Family resemblance plus 'regression to the mean'.

Real genetics is much richer than 'dominant masks recessive'.
items.why: Mendel's laws are presented as universal. They describe a subset of inheritance patterns. Even simple breeding shows the laws don't always apply directly.

items.title: Information can flow from RNA back to DNA
items.claim: Crick's central dogma: DNA makes RNA makes protein. The arrow goes one way: DNA to RNA. But retroviruses — including HIV — carry an enzyme that copies their RNA genome back into DNA.
items.prompt: What does reverse transcription mean for the dogma?

options.text: The central dogma is wrong and discredited

Crick's original statement was about residue-level sequence transfer; reverse transcription does flow RNA-to-DNA, but the forbidden flow (protein-to-DNA) has never been observed — the dogma is more nuanced than the textbook version
Reverse transcription is a lab artefact

items.reveal_title: Crick's original dogma was more sophisticated than the cartoon
items.reveal:
Crick (1958) explicitly listed which residue-level transfers were possible (DNA to DNA, DNA to RNA, RNA to protein) and which were special transfers (RNA to RNA, RNA to DNA) — possible but not normally done. He also listed forbidden transfers (anything starting from protein).

Reverse transcriptase, discovered by Temin and Baltimore in 1970 (1975 Nobel), is the canonical 'special transfer'. HIV uses it to integrate into the host genome. Some retrotransposons in our own genomes do it constantly.

The forbidden transfers (protein to DNA, protein to RNA, protein to protein) remain forbidden. The dogma, taken literally as Crick wrote it, still stands.
items.why: Pop science presents 'the central dogma' as a rigid one-way arrow. The real dogma is a constraint on which directions sequence information can flow in, and reverse transcription was always allowed.
